abstract: This study presents FiLLM, a Filipino-optimized large language model, designed to enhance natural language processing (NLP) capabilities in the Filipino language. Built upon the SeaLLM-7B 2.5 model, FiLLM leverages Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) finetuning to optimize memory efficiency while maintaining taskspecific performance. The model was trained and evaluated on diverse Filipino datasets to address key NLP tasks, including Named Entity Recognition (NER), Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging, Dependency Parsing, and Text Summarization. Performance comparisons with the CalamanCy model were conducted using F1 Score, Precision, Recall, Compression Rate, and Keyword Overlap metrics. Results indicate that Calamancy outperforms FILLM in several aspects, demonstrating its effectiveness in processing Filipino text with improved linguistic comprehension and adaptability. This research contributes to the advancement of Filipino NLP applications by providing an optimized, efficient, and scalable language model tailored for local linguistic needs.

content.problem: Large language models for the Filipino language remain underdeveloped because labeled Filipino datasets and computational resources are scarce.
content.proposed_solution: The authors build FiLLM by applying LoRA fine-tuning to the SeaLLM-7B 2.5 model on Filipino datasets, then compare it with CalamanCy on several NLP tasks.
content.algorithm_or_model: FiLLM, a LoRA fine-tuned SeaLLM-7B 2.5 model

content.claim: FiLLM performs well on Named Entity Recognition and Part-of-Speech tagging, but CalamanCy significantly outperforms it overall, especially on Dependency Parsing.
author_stated_limitations: Dependency parsing is the weakest task, showing the model still struggles with Filipino syntax.
Summarization performance may vary with the complexity and quality of the input text.
The practical importance of the statistically significant performance gap still needs to be evaluated for real use cases.
The quality and variability of the evaluation data may have influenced the observed outcomes.
Differences in methodology and group characteristics may affect the comparison in ways the statistical test does not capture.

evidence.problem_quote: Despite the increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in natural language processing (NLP), the development of large language models (LLMs) for Filipino remains limited due to the scarcity of labeled datasets and computational resources [9].
evidence.proposed_solution_quote: This linguistic gap has motivated the development of FiLLM, a Filipino-optimized large language model fine-tuned using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). This study aims to evaluate FiLLM's performance on key NLP tasks, comparing it with CalamanCy, an existing Filipino NLP model.
evidence.claim_quote: Results indicate that Calamancy outperforms FILLM in several aspects, demonstrating its effectiveness in processing Filipino text with improved linguistic comprehension and adaptability.
author_stated_limitation_quotes: However, Dependency Parsing remains a challenge, with precision and recall both at 71%, suggesting the need for improvements in handling Filipino syntax.
